subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add first-progress/startup-failed as a durable core lifecycle contract for sub-agent startup failures, or solve the hang with narrower internal timeout/status handling?
rationale: The source-reproducible problem is real, but the proposed fix changes observable lifecycle semantics across gateway, SDK, session, and subagent consumers, which requires maintainer API/product intent before an automated repair is safe.

options.title: Adopt lifecycle contract
options.body: Accept `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` as additive lifecycle phases and require a fresh current-main implementation across all active consumers.

options.title: Keep it internal
options.body: Fix sub-agent startup abort classification without adding public lifecycle phases, preserving the current event surface but giving less external observability.

options.title: Defer API change
options.body: Leave the issue open as a product backlog item until maintainers decide the broader lifecycle event model.

recommendation.title: Adopt lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Accept `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` as additive lifecycle phases and require a fresh current-main implementation across all active consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent lifecycle and terminal-outcome history makes this the best available owner for the API/product shape decision.
